N-1.1-A.skill: decide how subtracting a function from a constant changes both its direction and its concavity, using successive changes in a table rather than the direction alone.

N-1.1-B.skill: combine the direction and concavity of two functions to decide which features of their sum are forced and which are not.

N-1.2-A.skill: combine the average rates over two adjacent unequal intervals into the average rate over the union, weighting by interval length.

N-1.2-B.skill: work backward from a given average rate of change of a quadratic to a missing coefficient, tracking the cancellation of the constant and the division by interval width.

N-1.3-A.skill: infer concavity from average rates over intervals of unequal width, not from raw changes in output.

N-1.3-B.skill: locate local extrema from the sign changes in a list of average rates over consecutive unit intervals, without over-claiming an exact location.

N-1.4-A.skill: extend a table of a cubic by propagating the constant third difference back through second and first differences, rejecting lower-degree extrapolations.

N-1.4-B.skill: combine the turning-point bound (degree at least turning points plus one) with the parity forced by end behavior to find the least possible degree.

N-1.5-A.skill: count real zeros of a real-coefficient polynomial by adding the conjugate of every nonreal zero with its multiplicity before subtracting from the degree.

N-1.5-B.skill: use the factor theorem to find an unknown coefficient, then use the sum of the zeros of a monic cubic to get the sum of the remaining two without finding them.

N-1.6-A.skill: find the end behavior of a product with a reflected factor by tracking both the degree parity and the sign contributed by the reflection.

N-1.6-B.skill: build a sign chart from end behavior and zero multiplicities, changing sign only at odd-multiplicity zeros.

N-1.7-A.skill: find the horizontal asymptote of an unexpanded rational function with equal degrees by multiplying the leading coefficients of every factor, including the square.

N-1.7-B.skill: describe the side of the horizontal asymptote y = 0 that a rational function approaches at each end by tracking the sign of the ratio of leading terms through the parity of the degree gap.
